data_description.weather_compensation_enabled: Adds a proactive power contribution based on outdoor temperature, on top of PID's reactive correction (a classic “heating curve”) — was always on before this setting existed, so it defaults to enabled.
data_description.ff_reference_outdoor_temp: Outdoor temperature at/above which weather compensation contributes nothing. Default 15°C.
data_description.ff_weight: Extra power fraction added per °C the outdoor temperature is below the reference. Default 0.02.
data_description.ff_max_contribution: Cap — weather compensation alone never adds more than this fraction of power. Default 0.3 (30%).
data_description.outdoor_temp_sensor: Local weather station or outdoor module (e.g. Netatmo, Aqara). Overrides the weather entity temperature for adaptive away setpoint and season detection. Leave blank to use the weather entity.
data_description.outdoor_humidity_sensor: Local outdoor humidity sensor (e.g. Netatmo outdoor module). Used to weight mold-risk calculations more heavily when outdoor humidity is high.
data_description.precipitation_sensor: Rain/precipitation sensor (mm or mm/h). When it reports rain, an open window is always treated as pure heat loss regardless of CO₂ level — nobody ventilates on purpose in the rain.
data_description.wind_speed_sensor: Local wind speed sensor (m/s). Above 6 m/s, the window open-delay is shortened so heat loss is caught faster in blustery weather.
data_description.window_delay_default_min: How long a window must be open before Heat Manager actually turns off the heat in that room. Applies to every room — shortened automatically in strong wind or rain. Replaces the old per-room field, which was never editable from the panel.
data_description.window_off_temp: The setpoint sent to a room's TRV once its window-open delay has passed. Deliberately independent of “Away temperature for this room” (room step), which still floors the PID's own idle output and the night setback.
data_description.night_setback_enabled: When enabled, the PID target temperature is reduced by the setback value during the configured night hours. Uses the existing night start/end hours.
data_description.night_setback_temp: Degrees Celsius subtracted from the room's target temperature during night hours. The setpoint will not go below the room's away temperature.
data_description.house_voice_enabled: Requires the House Voice integration to be installed. When enabled, Heat Manager will announce events such as boost activation, season changes, and controller state changes.
data_description.pause_duration_min: How long the controller stays paused after a manual pause, before automatically resuming.
data_description.boost_default_temp: Used by heat_manager.boost_start / the panel's boost button when no temperature is specified. Default 24°C.
data_description.boost_default_minutes: Used by heat_manager.boost_start / the panel's boost button when no duration is specified. Default 30 minutes.
data_description.pid_enabled: When disabled, TRVs follow the Netatmo/Zigbee schedule directly with no proportional adjustment.
data_description.pid_kp: Proportional gain — higher values react more aggressively to temperature error. Default 0.5.
data_description.pid_ki: Integral gain — corrects a persistent offset over time. Default 0.02. Keep small; large values cause overshoot.
data_description.pid_kd: Derivative gain — reacts to the rate of change. Disabled (0) by default: TRVs have several minutes of thermal lag, so a derivative term mostly amplifies sensor noise.
data_description.trv_max_temp: TRV setpoint sent when PID power is at 100%. Default 28°C.
data_description.indoor_wake_sensor: Shared indoor temperature sensor used to detect the gentler WAKING phase during spring/autumn. Falls back to full ACTIVE heating when not set.
data_description.indoor_wake_threshold: Indoor temperature above which the system enters the WAKING phase instead of full ACTIVE heating. Default 21°C.
data_description.wake_setback_temp: Degrees Celsius subtracted from every room's setpoint while in the WAKING phase. Default 2°C.

data.door_styled_sensors: Show as door instead of window (cosmetic)
data.heated_door_sensors: Doors to a heated area (no heat cutoff)
data.window_delay_min: Window open delay (minutes) — unused, see global settings

data_description.door_styled_sensors: Optional subset of the Window / door sensors above that should be labelled and logged as a door instead of a window — purely cosmetic, the exact same grace period / off-temperature / 30-minute warning behaviour applies either way (e.g. a balcony door still loses heat like a window). A sensor must ALSO be selected above in Window / door sensors for this to have any effect — selecting it ONLY here does nothing.
data_description.heated_door_sensors: A SEPARATE list from Window / door sensors above — exterior doors leading to a heated/enclosed space (e.g. a front door onto a heated stairwell), not the outside air. These get NO heat-suppression behaviour at all: no grace period, no off-temperature, no warning — visibility and event log only. Do not add a sensor here INSTEAD of Window / door sensors if you want opening it to actually reduce heating.
data_description.window_delay_min: No longer read since v0.33.0 — every room's window open-delay now uses the single global setting instead (Season & global settings step). Left here only so a value already saved for this room isn't silently discarded; safe to ignore.
data_description.comfort_temp: PID target temperature for this room — authoritative for every TRV type, Netatmo included. Default 20°C.
data_description.co2_sensor: Used for context-aware window notifications and energy waste classification. When CO₂ is high, an open window is marked as ventilation rather than heat loss.
data_description.co2_threshold: CO₂ level above which an open window is classified as intentional ventilation. Default is 900 ppm. Increase for bedrooms (higher tolerance) or decrease for seldom-occupied rooms.
data_description.room_temp_sensor: Independent room probe for PID temperature feedback. Recommended for Zigbee TRVs whose built-in sensor sits on the radiator body (typically reads 1–3°C too high).
data_description.battery_sensor: TRV battery level sensor (sensor.* reporting %). Recommended for Zigbee TRVs, whose battery is usually its own entity rather than an attribute on the climate entity. Leave blank to fall back to the climate entity's own battery_level attribute, if it has one.
data_description.humidity_sensor: Relative humidity sensor (%) for this room. Used together with the room temperature sensor to calculate mold risk (dewpoint vs. surface temperature).
data_description.schedule_entity: A schedule.* helper or calendar.* entity. While a time block or event is active, its temperature overrides this room's normal target.

The climate entity `{climate_id}` configured for room **{room_name}** does not exist in Home Assistant. Heat Manager cannot control heating for this room until the entity is available.

To resolve: check that the integration providing `{climate_id}` is loaded and the entity ID is correct. Reload Heat Manager once the entity is available.
